data: India's first home-grown cryogenic engine — the LVM3 upper stage
Engine registry (PRD-032). Public-source nominal specs; ISRO imagery.
India's first home-grown cryogenic engine, born from necessity

When technology-transfer restrictions blocked India from acquiring cryogenic engine technology in the early 1990s, ISRO's Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre developed one from the ground up. The CE-20 is the result: a gas-generator cycle burning LOX and LH2 that powers the upper stage of LVM3, India's heaviest operational rocket. It first flew on 5 June 2017 on the GSLV Mk III D1 developmental flight, capping a two-decade development program that turned a geopolitical barrier into independent capability. The CE-20 is the engine that will carry Gaganyaan — India's first crewed mission — to orbit.
